course_title: IC Design Process: Beginner's Overview to VLSI

slides.title: Course Overview: IC Design
points: Connects HDL to actual silicon circuit.
Covers RTL, verification, synthesis, physical design, manufacturing.
slides.speaker_notes: Welcome to IC Design Process, a beginner's overview of VLSI. This course simplifies the common problem of connecting your hardware description language code to the actual silicon circuit. We'll explore the theoretical foundations behind RTL design, functional verification, synthesis, physical design, and manufacturing, without focusing on specific coding.

slides.title: What are ICs and SOCs?
points: IC: Electronic circuits on tiny semiconductor plate.
SOC: Complete system on a single chip.
Billions of transistors in a tiny space.
slides.speaker_notes: An Integrated Circuit, or IC, is a device with numerous electronic circuits built onto a tiny silicon plate, capable of holding billions of transistors. A System-on-Chip, or SOC, takes this further by integrating an entire electronic system onto a single chip. While designs differ, manufacturing for both analog and digital ICs is quite similar, and this course focuses on digital IC processes.

slides.title: Evolution of VLSI Technology
points: Growth through MSI, LSI to billions of transistors.
slides.speaker_notes: IC technology rapidly evolved from fabricating just a few components in the 1960s, known as Small-Scale Integration or SSI, to thousands, then tens of thousands in the 70s, designated LSI. By the 2000s, chips housed billions of transistors. Today, irrespective of the exact count, all advanced IC manufacturing is broadly termed Very Large-Scale Integration, or VLSI.

slides.title: Digital Circuit Fundamentals
slides.speaker_notes: Before designing ICs, remember digital circuits convert real-world data into binary. Transistors act as fundamental switches, turning voltage on and off to process these 0s and 1s. Circuits are categorized as combinational, where output depends only on current inputs, or sequential, which include memory elements and depend on input history.

slides.title: Building Blocks: Gates & Flip-Flops
points: Digital circuits use logic gates (AND, OR, NOT...).
All digital circuits ultimately built from transistors.
slides.speaker_notes: Digital circuits are constructed from logic gates like AND, OR, and NOT, which perform basic boolean operations. For memory, we use flip-flops, capable of storing a single bit. Crucially, all flip-flops are built from logic gates, and all logic gates are fundamentally made using transistors. So, every digital circuit boils down to a vast array of transistors.

slides.title: Abstraction with HDLs
points: Complex circuits involve billions of transistors.
slides.speaker_notes: Given that modern digital circuits involve billions of transistors, designing at that level is simply impractical. This is where Hardware Description Languages, or HDLs, come in. HDLs allow us to model complex digital circuits at a higher, more abstract level, effectively hiding the intricate transistor-level details and simplifying the entire design process.
